chief_complaint: tender, red, painful swelling on the side of the nose below the inner corner of the eye with pus expressing from punctum
hpi_details: 62F presenting with acute erythema and indurated swelling over the inferomedial canthal lacrimal sac area where pressure expresses thick purulent discharge from the lower punctum requiring oral cephalexin and warm compresses.
ideas: She thinks a clogged pore or an ingrown hair beside her nose has turned into a deep, infected boil.
concerns: She is worried that the infection will spread directly into her eyeball and permanently ruin her eyesight.
expectations: She hopes to receive a prescription for strong oral antibiotics and find out if the swelling needs to be drained.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

must_ask.say: Can you show me exactly where the swelling and tenderness are?

must_ask.objective: Ask about discharge from the tear duct area
must_ask.say: Have you noticed pus or discharge from near your tear duct?
Have you had excessive tearing or a blocked tear duct before this started?

must_ask.objective: Screen for fever or spreading redness
must_ask.say: Do you have a fever, spreading redness, any change in vision, or pain when moving the eye?

history.answer: About three days ago, a painful red lump appeared on the side of my nose just below the inner corner of my left eye, and today some yellow pus started oozing out when I touched it.
The swelling began three days ago as a small tender bump, but over the last day it has become much larger, redder, and more painful.
The skin on the left side of my nose right below the eye corner is very red, and the white part of my eye is slightly pink right near that corner.
It feels like a constant, throbbing ache, and it hurts intensely whenever anything touches it.
The lump is right over the side of my nose, just under the inner corner of my left eye.
Yes, when I gently touched the swollen area this morning, thick yellow pus oozed out from the tiny opening on my lower eyelid.
For the past few months, my left eye has been constantly watering and tearing up, even when I wasn't crying.
No, my vision is completely normal and clear in both eyes, aside from having to wipe away tears.
No, bright light does not bother me or cause any eye discomfort.
No, I have not noticed rainbow halos around lights, and I do not have a headache or any nausea.
No, it does not itch at all; it just aches and throbs.
The eyelid itself is not swollen and there are no bumps on the lash line, only that swollen lump on the side of my nose.
No, looking up, down, or side to side does not cause any pain.
No, my eye does not feel pushed forward, and I am not seeing double.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, I haven't had a cold, congestion, or runny nose lately, and no one around me has had an eye infection.
No, I have never used contact lenses; I only wear glasses for reading.
No, I did not injure my eye, get hit in the face, or get any chemicals or dust in it.
No, I don't get seasonal allergies, hay fever, or allergic rashes.
No, my eyes are not dry at all—my left eye actually waters too much—and my mouth is not dry.
No, I don't have morning back stiffness, aching joints, mouth sores, or persistent diarrhea.
No, I haven't had any rash, sores, or blisters on my forehead or the tip of my nose.
No, I haven't had violent coughing or vomiting, and I do not take any blood thinners or aspirin.
I have never had glaucoma, eye surgery, or serious eye infections, just the persistent tearing from that left eye recently.
I thought a blocked pore or a pimple near the corner of my eye must have gotten infected and turned into a boil.
I'm really scared the infection is going to spread into my eyeball and cause me to go blind.
I have had high blood pressure for about five years and mild cholesterol issues.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day in the morning for my blood pressure.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink a single glass of wine on occasional weekends.

exam.finding: Temperature 37.0°C, blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

An erythematous, tense, fluctuant swelling measuring approximately 1.5 cm is present over the left inferomedial canthus and side of the nose, and gentle pressure over the lacrimal sac expresses thick purulent discharge from the inferior punctum.
Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes; pupils are equal, round, and briskly reactive to light; extraocular movements are full without pain or diplopia, and no proptosis is observed.
Mild localized conjunctival injection at the left nasal corner, with normal sclera, clear corneas bilaterally, and no foreign bodies identified upon eyelid eversion.
No palpation or percussion tenderness over the frontal, ethmoid, or maxillary sinuses bilaterally.
No palpable lymphadenopathy in the preauricular, submandibular, or anterior cervical chains.
